title: Sections of the inverse image to a directed limit of spectral spaces over a quasi-compact open are a colimit
statement: Let $I$ be a directed set (nonempty, any two elements have a common upper bound), let $(X_i)_{i\in I}$ be spectral spaces [def-weil-spectral-space] and for $i\le i'$ let $f_{ii'}:X_{i'}\to X_i$ be spectral maps (continuous, with $f_{ii'}^{-1}(W)$ quasi-compact for every quasi-compact open $W\subseteq X_i$), with $f_{ii}=\mathrm{id}$ and $f_{ii'}\circ f_{i'i''}=f_{ii''}$ for $i\le i'\le i''$. Let $X$ be a topological space with continuous maps $p_i:X\to X_i$, $f_{ii'}\circ p_{i'}=p_i$, which is a limit of the system in the category of topological spaces (the map $x\mapsto(p_i(x))_i$ is a bijection of $X$ onto $\{(x_i)\in\prod_iX_i: f_{ii'}(x_{i'})=x_i\text{ for }i\le i'\}$ and the topology of $X$ is the coarsest for which all $p_i$ are continuous). For a continuous map $h$ let $h^{-1}$ be the inverse image of sheaves of sets with unit $\eta^h$ on sections, as in [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image] (2), (3) with values in sets, and for continuous maps $h,h'$ let $c:h'^{-1}h^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}(h\circ h')^{-1}$ be the isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-inverse-image-composition]. Fix $i\in I$, a sheaf of sets $\mathcal G$ on $X_i$ and a quasi-compact open $U_i\subseteq X_i$. For $i'\ge i$ put $\mathcal G_{i'}=f_{ii'}^{-1}\mathcal G$ and $U_{i'}=f_{ii'}^{-1}(U_i)$ (so $p_{i'}^{-1}(U_{i'})=p_i^{-1}(U_i)$), let $\rho_{i'}:\mathcal G_{i'}(U_{i'})\to(p_i^{-1}\mathcal G)(p_i^{-1}U_i)$ be $c_{\mathcal G}\circ\eta^{p_{i'}}_{\mathcal G_{i'},U_{i'}}$ with $c:p_{i'}^{-1}f_{ii'}^{-1}\mathcal G\xrightarrow{\sim}(f_{ii'}\circ p_{i'})^{-1}\mathcal G=p_i^{-1}\mathcal G$, and for $i\le i'\le i''$ let $\rho_{i''i'}:\mathcal G_{i'}(U_{i'})\to\mathcal G_{i''}(U_{i''})$ be $c_{\mathcal G}\circ\eta^{f_{i'i''}}_{\mathcal G_{i'},U_{i'}}$ with $c:f_{i'i''}^{-1}f_{ii'}^{-1}\mathcal G\xrightarrow{\sim}f_{ii''}^{-1}\mathcal G$. Then (a) $\rho_{i'i'}=\mathrm{id}$, $\rho_{i''}\circ\rho_{i''i'}=\rho_{i'}$ and $\rho_{i'''i''}\circ\rho_{i''i'}=\rho_{i'''i'}$ for $i\le i'\le i''\le i'''$; (b) every $s\in(p_i^{-1}\mathcal G)(p_i^{-1}U_i)$ equals $\rho_{i'}(t)$ for some $i'\ge i$ and some $t\in\mathcal G_{i'}(U_{i'})$; (c) if $t,t'\in\mathcal G_{i'}(U_{i'})$ and $\rho_{i'}(t)=\rho_{i'}(t')$, then $\rho_{i''i'}(t)=\rho_{i''i'}(t')$ for some $i''\ge i'$. In other words $(p_i^{-1}\mathcal G)(p_i^{-1}U_i)=\varinjlim_{i'\ge i}(f_{ii'}^{-1}\mathcal G)(f_{ii'}^{-1}U_i)$.

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma Tag 0A32 (label lemma-compute-pullback-to-limit, line 3565) with its proof, stated there for a cofiltered index category; a directed set is the special case used here; the transition maps of the colimit are the pullback maps composed with the canonical isomorphisms of Lemma Tag 008I

proof.text: Step 1 (canonical maps and their uniqueness). For continuous maps A --f--> B --g--> C, let c be the unique composition isomorphism compatible with the adjunction units [lem-weil-pbc-sets-inverse-image-composition]. The morphism u(f,g):g^{-1}G -> f_*(fg)^{-1}G is the unit for f followed by f_*(c). Its composite with the unit for g is the unit for fg. The adjunction g^{-1} left adjoint to g_* [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image] makes this equation determine u(f,g) uniquely. Hence u(f,g) followed by f_*u(h,fg) equals u(hf,g), since their composites with the unit for g are the same. The same uniqueness proves u(id,g)=id. Transport along the given equalities of maps and evaluate on sections. The specified HEq formulas identify these maps with rho and transition, proving all three identities in (a).

Step 2 (the unit on stalks). For a continuous map q and sheaf H define the stalk map H_{q(x)} -> (q^{-1}H)_x by the unit followed by the stalk-pushforward map. It sends the germ of t to the germ of its unit image. The presheaf inverse-image stalk isomorphism and the sheafification stalk isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-sets-inverse-image-stalk] show that this is bijective: identify the abstract sheaf pullback with the sheafification of the presheaf pullback using uniqueness of left adjoints and its unit equation. Equality of morphisms from a stalk is checked on germs. Composition with a sheaf isomorphism preserves these tests.

Step 3 (limit topology). Extract injectivity and surjectivity of the tuple map from the unique-point limit hypothesis. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-spectral-directed-limit-spectral] to obtain that X is spectral and every p_j is spectral. Compact opens therefore have compact inverse images. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-spectral-limit-descend-opens] for descent of compact opens and inclusions.

Step 4 (eventual equality on any compact open). Let W be compact open at stage j and t,t' sections of a sheaf H on W whose unit images along p_j agree. At every x above W their germs at p_j(x) agree by Step 2. Equality of germs gives an open neighbourhood on which their restrictions agree [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise]. Refine each such neighbourhood to a compact open contained in W [def-weil-spectral-space]. Compactness of p_j^{-1}(W) selects finitely many, whose union V is compact open, satisfies V subset W, and p_j^{-1}(W) subset p_j^{-1}(V); all germs of t,t' on V agree. Inclusion descent from Step 3 gives k >= j with f_jk^{-1}(W) subset f_jk^{-1}(V). Step 2 gives equality of the pulled-back germs everywhere on f_jk^{-1}(W), hence equality of the unit images by [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-sections-determined-by-germs]. A sheaf isomorphism in the composition comparison preserves equality, so this proves (c), and the same result for every compact open at stage j.

Step 5 (finite local representatives). Given s on p_i^{-1}(U), lift each germ of s by the surjective unit stalk map of Step 2. Every lifted germ is represented by a section of G on an open neighbourhood [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise]. Refine this neighbourhood to a compact open V contained in U and restrict its representative. Equality of germs gives a neighbourhood of x on which the unit image agrees with s. Refine it to a compact open W contained in p_i^{-1}(V). Compactness of p_i^{-1}(U) gives a finite family W_l covering it, with compact opens V_l subset U and sections t_l of G(V_l) representing s on W_l. The finite index type may be empty; no nonemptiness assumption excludes the empty open.

Step 6 (descend the finite cover). Descend every W_l by compact-open descent [lem-weil-pbc-spectral-limit-descend-opens], and use directedness to pull them all to one stage j >= i. Descend the finitely many inclusions W_l subset p_i^{-1}(V_l) and pass to another common upper bound. At this stage the union C of the descended compact opens lies in U_j, and their pullbacks cover p_j^{-1}(U_j). Descend the inclusion p_j^{-1}(U_j) subset p_j^{-1}(C) once more. Pulling the family to that stage gives compact opens T_l with union U_j, T_l subset f_ij^{-1}(V_l), and p_j^{-1}(T_l)=W_l. Finite upper bounds are constructed by induction on finite sets, so this also handles an empty family.

Step 7 (agreement and gluing). Restrict the unit images of the t_l to T_l, obtaining sections v_l of G_j. The composition-unit equation and naturality with restriction identify their rho-images with the restrictions of s. Therefore their restrictions to every T_l intersection T_m have equal rho-images. These intersections are compact open [def-weil-spectral-space], so Step 4 makes each pair agree at a later stage. A finite common upper bound makes every pair agree simultaneously; Step 1 ensures that equality persists on passing to that upper bound. The sheaf gluing axiom gives a section on U_k. Naturality, the composition laws of Step 1 and local equality with s show its image is s. This proves (b), completing all displayed clauses.
